title: Piano Roll Tricks
intro: The Piano Roll is where MIDI becomes music. These are the editing moves that make it fast.

tips.t: Select all notes of the same pitch in one click
tips.d: Click a key on the keyboard graphic at the left of the Piano Roll and every note at that pitch in the region is selected. Perfect for grabbing all the hi‑hats at once.

src.label: Apple — Select notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

tips.t: Change note length numerically in the Event Float
tips.d: Open the Event Float window with Window > Show Event Float, or press ⌥E. It shows the selected note as one line in the same format as the Event List, and you can type new values straight in, length included.

src.label: Apple — Use the Event Float window in Logic Pro for Mac
Studio Interns — Show/Hide Event Float ⌥E, Logic Pro keyboard command of the day
Logic Pro GEM — Fader Event: A MIDI Event Wannabe

tips.t: Force legato to fix gappy pads
tips.d: Select the notes, then choose Edit > Trim > Note End to Following Notes (Force Legato) in the Piano Roll. Every note extends to end where the next one begins, and pads and basslines stop sounding stuttery instantly.

src.label: 9to5Mac — The Logic Pros: 3 helpful tricks to streamline your MIDI/audio editing
Your Local Musician — Logic Pro X Tutorial: Force Legato
Apple — Resize notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.d: Select the notes and choose Edit > Trim > Note End to Remove Overlaps to Following Notes (8 Ticks Gap) in the Piano Roll. Logic shortens the note ends so nothing overlaps, leaving an eight-tick gap before the next note. A Selected Notes version does the same job measured only against the other selected notes.

src.label: Apple — Resize notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.d: Hold ⌥ while dragging any note or selection to copy rather than move — you can even ⌥-drag notes between two Piano Roll windows, or between two different projects. To stop a drag changing pitch, turn on Logic Pro > Settings > General > Editing > "Limit Dragging to One Direction In Piano Roll and Score": the direction you start in is then the only one you can move in. Pressing ⇧ while dragging switches that behaviour on and off; it is not a pitch lock on its own.

src.label: Apple — Copy notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Move notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Place a note between grid divisions
tips.d: Set the Snap pop-up menu to Ticks, which snaps to 1/3840 of a beat, or press Control-Shift as you drag to move the note in tick steps, overriding the Snap value. You can also switch snapping off with the On/Off button beside the Snap pop-up menu.

src.label: Apple — Snap items to the grid in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Move notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Change velocity by dragging with the Velocity tool
tips.d: Pick the Velocity tool from the Tool menu, or hold Control-Command to turn the Pointer into it temporarily, then drag up or down on a note. A help tag shows the velocity as you drag. Choose View > Set Note Color > By Velocity if you want the note colour to track it too.

src.label: Apple — Edit velocity in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Change a selection's velocity without flattening it
tips.d: Select the notes, then drag one of them vertically with the Velocity tool, or drag the Velocity slider in the Piano Roll header. Logic keeps the relative differences between the notes' velocities. When any note hits 0 or 127, the rest stop too. Hold ⌥ while dragging to override this.

src.label: Apple — Edit velocity in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Show the automation lane inside the Piano Roll
tips.d: Click the Show/Hide Automation button in the Piano Roll Editor menu bar, then choose a parameter from the Automation/MIDI Parameter pop-up menu. Its MIDI or automation data appears in a lane under the notes, where you can edit it. Track automation shown there is the same curve as in the Tracks area, so edits appear in both places.

src.label: Apple — The Automation/MIDI area in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Colour notes by velocity to read dynamics instantly
tips.d: In the Piano Roll's View menu, set note colour to Velocity. Flat parts become visibly, obviously flat.

src.label: Apple — Edit velocity in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Quantise from the region inspector, not destructively
tips.d: The Quantize field in the Region inspector is non‑destructive and can be dialled back or removed at any point. Use it before you ever use the destructive version.

src.label: Apple — Quantize parameter values in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use Q‑Strength to keep the human feel
tips.d: Under the region's more‑options triangle, Q‑Strength at 60 to 80 percent pulls notes toward the grid without gluing them to it.

src.label: Apple — Advanced quantization parameters in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Quantise only the notes that need it
tips.d: Select the offending notes in the Piano Roll and quantise the selection rather than the whole region. The good parts of the take stay untouched.

src.label: Apple — Quantize the timing of notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)
